intro: You are in Alanya Museum, in Antalya province, opened in 1967. Here the town's Roman and Seljuk layers are shown side by side. Its best known pieces are the sarcophagi in its garden and a small bronze statuette of Herakles.
history: Opened in 1967, the museum gathers finds that run from the Roman Coracesium to the Seljuk Alaiye. Sarcophagi, capitals and Ottoman gravestones line its garden, while inside, the halls hold material from the town's past as a harbour and shipyard.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Bronze Herakles statuette and the Sarcophagus garden. Then explore the Seljuk section and the Ethnography hall.
facts: Did you know? The bronze Herakles of the second century AD is reckoned the finest object ever found at Alanya, and it is only 52 centimetres tall. Out in the garden, the sarcophagi and Ottoman gravestones set the town's layers side by side, from Roman Coracesium to Seljuk Alaiye.
outro: This brings our tour of Alanya Museum to an end. Please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these pieces stay safe for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
